text.p: These are the highlights of the main stories in the Bosnian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- U.S. envoy Robert Gelbard will visit Bosnia on Sunday or Monday to monitor the political crisis in the Serb entity and to continue talks with government officials on the return of refugees to Mostar and the design of a common currency

- A working group formed by the office of the High Representative will prepare a proposal for the design of a new Bosnian flag and coat of arms. According to an unnamed source from the High Representative's office, the flag will not contain any national symbols or the traditional Bosnian lily.

- A newspaper poll says 38 percent of the public favour the use of common symbols from Bosnian history and culture for a new flag and coat of arms. It said 32 percent believe only neutral or non-nationalist symbols should be employed. Only eight percent favour the use of religious symbols from the three national communities.

- Bosnian Moslems recently expelled from the town of Jajce will go back to their homes by August 25, said Gerd Wagner of the High Representative's office. The first group of Bosnians will go back to the village of Kruscica, near Jajce.

- The town of Jajce has been a typical example of "ethnic engineering" and the agreement on the return of Moslem refugees to Jajce is an important test of Croat and Moslem relations inside the federation, a newspaper commentary says. -- Sarajevo Newsroom, +387-71-663-864
